Integrated species distribution model with physiological limits

sdm_integrated.Rd

sdm_integrated() fits one niche model to two kinds of data at once (Fithian et al. 2015; Isaac et al. 2020):

  • presence-only records (for example GBIF), modelled as an inhomogeneous Poisson point process with background (quadrature) points, with its own intercept and optional bias covariates that describe where people look (distance to roads, towns, field stations);

  • presence-absence surveys (for example standardised elevational transects), modelled with a complementary log-log link, so that the probability of presence at a site of area \(A\) is \(1 - \exp(-A \lambda(x))\).

Both share the same environmental response \(\lambda(x)\), so the many but biased presence-only records and the few but unbiased surveys inform one niche: the surveys correct the sampling bias of the records and the records fill in where no surveys were made.

Two constraints keep projections to future climates biologically plausible:

  • unimodal: the response to these covariates is forced to be a hump (negative quadratic term), so suitability falls beyond the optimum instead of rising without limit in novel climates;

  • limits: physiological limits, such as a critical thermal maximum (CTmax) for maximum temperature. Suitability is multiplied by a smooth step that falls from 0.9 to 0.1 over the limit_width just inside the limit, and towards 0 beyond it.

Covariates are standardised before fitting, and a small ridge penalty (lambda) stabilises the fit; the coefficients are reported on the standardised scale.

Usage

sdm_integrated(
  presence,
  background,
  area,
  survey = NULL,
  covariates,
  quadratic = covariates,
  unimodal = character(),
  bias = character(),
  limits = list(),
  limit_width = 1,
  lambda = 0.01
)

# S3 method for class 'tmr_sdm_integrated'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  type = c("probability", "intensity", "link"),
  site_area = 1,
  se_fit = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

presence

Data frame of covariates at presence-only records.

background

Data frame of covariates at background points spread over the study area (for example 10,000 random cells).

area

Total area of the study region (any unit; it scales the intensity of the presence-only process).

survey

Optional data frame of presence-absence surveys: covariates and a 0/1 column present (and optionally site_area, in the same units as area; default 1).

covariates

Environmental covariates (column names).

quadratic

Covariates that also get a squared term; default all.

unimodal

Quadratic covariates whose response must be a hump.

bias

Bias covariates, used only for the presence-only data. Set them to a common value (for example their minimum, meaning "well surveyed") when predicting.

limits

Named list of physiological limits, each c(lower, upper) on the original scale of the covariate (use NA for no limit), for example list(bio5 = c(NA, 33)) for a CTmax of 33 degrees C.

limit_width

Width of the smooth fall to zero at a limit, in the units of the covariate.

lambda

Ridge penalty on the environmental coefficients.

object

A fitted sdm_integrated() model.

newdata

Data frame or SpatRaster of covariates. Bias covariates are ignored (prediction is for unbiased sampling).

type

"probability", "intensity" or "link".

site_area

Area for type = "probability"; default 1 (one survey site).

se_fit

For a data frame newdata, also return the standard error of the linear predictor (se_link, by the delta method from the covariance of the fitted parameters) and a confidence interval formed on the link scale and back-transformed to type (lower, upper).

level

Confidence level of the interval.

...

Unused.

Value

sdm_integrated(): an object of class tmr_sdm_integrated with the coefficients (coef), their standard errors (se, from the inverse Hessian), the log-likelihood and the standardisation used. predict() gives, for a data frame or a SpatRaster of covariates, the probability of presence in an area of site_area (type = "probability"), the intensity ("intensity") or the linear predictor ("link").

References

Fithian, W., Elith, J., Hastie, T. and Keith, D. A. (2015). Bias correction in species distribution models: pooling survey and collection data for multiple species. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 6, 424-438.

Isaac, N. J. B. et al. (2020). Data integration for large-scale models of species distributions. Trends in Ecology & Evolution, 35, 56-67.

Sunday, J. M., Bates, A. E. and Dulvy, N. K. (2012). Thermal tolerance and the global redistribution of animals. Nature Climate Change, 2, 686-690.

See also

geo_shift_simulate() to add dispersal to the projections.

Examples

set.seed(1)
# Virtual species with an optimum at 20 C, records biased towards roads
bg <- data.frame(temp = runif(5000, 5, 30), road = runif(5000))
lam <- function(d) exp(2 - 0.08 * (d$temp - 20)^2)
keep <- runif(5000) < lam(bg) / max(lam(bg)) * exp(-3 * bg$road)
po <- bg[keep, ][1:300, ]
sv <- data.frame(temp = runif(80, 5, 30), road = runif(80))
sv$present <- rbinom(80, 1, 1 - exp(-0.02 * lam(sv)))
fit <- sdm_integrated(po, bg,
  area = 1000, survey = sv,
  covariates = "temp", unimodal = "temp", bias = "road",
  limits = list(temp = c(NA, 28))
)
fit
#> Integrated species distribution model
#> 300 presence-only records, 5000 background points, 80 survey sites
#> Physiological limits: "temp"
#>                  estimate     se
#> temp               3.0253 0.2900
#> temp^2            -4.4654 0.3490
#> po_intercept      -0.4739 0.0912
#> road              -0.7831 0.0680
#> survey_intercept  -2.2072 0.5811
predict(fit, data.frame(temp = c(10, 20, 27, 29), road = 0))
#> [1] 3.178927e-05 1.677707e-01 2.371421e-03 2.242139e-07
